newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields rise on US data, crown firms.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields rise on US data, crown firms.

text.p: Swedish bond yields rose on higher than expected U.S. employment figures on Friday.

The crown was boosted by a higher than expected November trade surplus of 12.7 billion crowns as well as by a stronger Norwegian crown and a generally weaker mark, dealers said. * Six month T-bill rates were up one basis point at 3.73 pct. * The nine-year bond yield rose four basis points at 6.76 pct. * The crown firmed to 4.3570 a mark vs 4.3930 late on Thursday.
STOCKHOLM, Jan 10 (Reuter) - Swedish bond yields rose on Friday after stronger-than-expected U.S. December jobs data, which triggered inflation fears and an upturn in interest rates.
The nine-year bond yield rose four basis points to 6.76 percent, while the six-month T-bill rates gained one basis point to 3.73 percent.
The crown was boosted by a stronger Norwegian crown and a generally weaker mark, as well as by a higher than expected November trade surplus of 12.5 billion crowns, dealers said.
Late on Friday, the crown was at 4.3570 a mark, down from 4.3930 late on Thursday.
According to dealers, the Riksbank intervened in the market which would be in line with its policy to smooth out sudden crown movements.
The bank sold crowns for marks around the level of 4.37 crowns a mark, dealers said.
"The volume was small and the Riksbank wanted to stop the strengthening in a turbulent international market," one dealer said.
The crown has appreciated sharply in the last few days, starting the four-day week at 4.4530 a mark.
